title: OpenCode HTTP Wait Endpoint Semantics Probe
summary: The FP-MCP-248 OpenCode HTTP wait endpoint semantics probe ran with cleanup enabled. It created one titled OpenCode session, submitted the tiny canary prompt through /session/{id}/prompt_async, called /api/session/{id}/wait once with a bounded timeout, read /session/{id}/message after wait, and deleted only the created canary session. The probe returned sessionCreated=true, promptAsyncSubmitted=true, promptAsyncHttpStatus=204, waitEndpointCalled=true, waitEndpointSucceeded=false, waitEndpointTimedOut=false, waitHttpStatus=503, waitContentType=application/json, messagesAfterWaitHttpStatus=200, messagesAfterWaitCount=2, assistantMessageCountAfterWait=1, assistantTextObservedAfterWait=false, canaryTextObservedAfterWait=false, sessionDeleted=true, deleteHttpStatus=200. This is a useful negative observation: /api/session/{id}/wait as invoked did not provide a successful completion boundary, while the message endpoint remained reachable after the wait failure.
caveats: The probe used POST /api/session/{id}/wait; the observed 503 may indicate wrong endpoint variant, wrong method, missing prerequisite state, or OpenCode server-side wait unavailability.
The message endpoint returned two messages and one assistant message after wait, but the current parser did not observe assistant text or the exact canary string in that response shape.
This does not invalidate the FP-MCP-247 result where message-based completion observed OPENCODE_HTTP_CANARY_OK without using wait.
Further inspection should compare message response shapes and possibly test documented non-api wait endpoint variants before using wait as a completion source.
